summary: Extends BGP to carry Autonomous System numbers as four-octet values instead of the two-octet encoding in the base specification. It obsoletes RFC 4893 and updates RFC 4271. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: The internet gave each network a number, but the original number size was running out. This memo makes the numbers longer so there are many more to give out.

questions: what is a four-octet as number
how do old and new bgp speakers interoperate
subtitle: How BGP grew from two-octet to four-octet AS numbers while old and new routers kept working together.

tldr.problem: The base BGP specification encodes the Autonomous System number as a two-octet entity, and the pool of two-octet numbers was expected to run out.
tldr.mechanism: A new capability lets BGP speakers announce four-octet AS support and carry four-octet numbers directly. Two optional transitive attributes, AS4_PATH and AS4_AGGREGATOR, carry the long numbers across speakers that do not understand them, and a reserved two-octet number, AS_TRANS, stands in for them.
tldr.outcome: Upgrades can happen gradually, one speaker at a time. This Proposed Standard obsoletes RFC 4893 and updates RFC 4271, and it also specifies error handling for the new attributes.

today: RFC 6793 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 4893 and updates RFC 4271. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Running Out of AS Numbers
sections.content:
In the base BGP specification (RFC 4271) the Autonomous System (AS) number is a two-octet entity. To prepare for the anticipated exhaustion of two-octet AS numbers, this document extends BGP to carry AS numbers as four-octet entities. The IANA pool of AS numbers grows from 0-65535 to 0-4294967295.

The design allows a gradual transition. It defines a BGP capability to signal four-octet support, plus two attributes that preserve four-octet path information across speakers that lack support. It also says how to rebuild the AS path from the old and new attributes.

RFC 6793 obsoletes RFC 4893 and updates RFC 4271. It adds clarifications, editorial changes and error handling for the new attributes.
sections.eli5: The phone company ran short of short phone numbers, so it adds longer ones. It has to make sure the old phones still work during the change.

sections.title: The Protocol Extensions
sections.content:
The RFC calls a speaker without the new support an OLD BGP speaker and one with it a NEW BGP speaker. AS numbers appear in the My Autonomous System field of OPEN, in the AS_PATH and AGGREGATOR attributes of UPDATE, and in the Communities attribute.

A NEW speaker advertises the four-octet AS number capability through BGP Capabilities Advertisements. The capability value carries the speaker's own AS number as four octets, with Capability Length 4. Between two NEW speakers, AS_PATH and AGGREGATOR keep their format but each AS number is four octets.

For paths crossing OLD speakers there are two optional transitive attributes. AS4_PATH has the same semantics and encoding as AS_PATH but with four-octet numbers, and the confederation segment types AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE and AS_CONFED_SET MUST NOT appear in it. AS4_AGGREGATOR is the four-octet form of AGGREGATOR.

An existing two-octet number becomes a four-octet number by setting the two high-order octets to zero, which is called mappable. Four-octet numbers that cannot be mapped are represented in two-octet fields by a reserved number, AS_TRANS. A NEW speaker without a globally unique two-octet AS number also places AS_TRANS in the My Autonomous System field of its OPEN message.
sections.eli5: Long house numbers are written on a second label for mail carriers who can read them. On the old short label, long numbers are replaced by one stand-in number so the old carriers still see something that fits.

sections.title: Two New Speakers Talking
sections.content:
When both ends advertise the capability, the rules are simple. On receiving the other side's OPEN, a NEW speaker MUST use the AS number from the capability value instead of the My Autonomous System field. Each side MUST encode AS numbers as four octets in AS_PATH and AGGREGATOR it sends and assume the same for what it receives.

AS4_PATH and AS4_AGGREGATOR MUST NOT be sent between NEW speakers. A NEW speaker that receives one from another NEW speaker MUST discard that attribute and continue processing the UPDATE.
sections.eli5: When both friends know the long numbers, they just use them and do not need the stand-in label.

sections.title: New Speakers Talking to Old Ones
sections.content:
Peering between a NEW and an OLD speaker is possible only if the NEW speaker has a two-octet AS number, and AS_TRANS MUST be used when it has none.

Sending. A NEW speaker sends the AS path in AS_PATH using two-octet numbers, with each non-mappable number replaced by AS_TRANS. This keeps the path length. It also sends the real path in AS4_PATH, unless every number is mappable, in which case it MUST NOT send AS4_PATH. Confederation segments are left out of AS4_PATH. If the aggregating AS has a non-mappable number, the speaker MUST send AS4_AGGREGATOR and set AGGREGATOR to AS_TRANS; if it is mappable, AS4_AGGREGATOR MUST NOT be sent. Because AS4_PATH is optional transitive, OLD speakers pass it along unchanged.

Receiving. If AGGREGATOR does not hold AS_TRANS, the AS4_AGGREGATOR and AS4_PATH are ignored. Otherwise AS4_AGGREGATOR describes the aggregator and the path must be reconstructed. The speaker counts AS numbers in AS_PATH and AS4_PATH. If AS_PATH has fewer, AS4_PATH is ignored. Otherwise it takes the leading part of AS_PATH and prepends it to AS4_PATH so the total matches the AS_PATH count.

The RFC warns that the path cannot always be rebuilt, for example when an OLD speaker aggregates routes whose AS4_PATH carries at least one real four-octet number.
sections.eli5: When talking to an old friend, you swap the long number for the stand-in and tuck the real numbers in a note. On the way back, you use the note to fix the address.

sections.title: Error Handling
sections.content:
The RFC picks the attribute discard approach: drop the bad attribute, log it and keep processing the UPDATE. It reasons that two-octet numbers dominate during the transition and sit in AS_PATH, and that AS4_AGGREGATOR is only informational.

An AS4_PATH is malformed if its length is not a multiple of two or is under 6, if a segment length is zero or inconsistent with the attribute length, or if a segment type is not one of AS_SEQUENCE, AS_SET, AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE and AS_CONFED_SET. An AS4_AGGREGATOR is malformed if its length is not 8. Confederation segments found in AS4_PATH from an OLD speaker are discarded and logged.
sections.eli5: If a note looks scrambled, you throw away the note, write down that it happened, and carry on reading the rest of the mail.

sections.title: Transition and Communities
sections.content:
An AS with a two-octet number may upgrade its speakers piecemeal. An AS that wants a four-octet number of its own can only do so after all its speakers support four-octet numbers. A non-mappable number cannot be a Confederation member AS number until all speakers in the Confederation have transitioned.

The Communities attribute encodes an AS number in two octets, so it cannot work for a non-mappable four-octet AS. Such speakers should use four-octet AS specific extended communities instead.

A MULTI_EXIT_DISC risk exists when an AS of OLD speakers peers with two or more NEW ASes that use AS_TRANS, because it may then influence route selection across different neighbors. Lost path information after aggregation by an OLD speaker is safe if the aggregate is less specific than every component route; in all other cases it creates the risk of a routing loop.
sections.eli5: A town can switch to long house numbers street by street. A house can use a long number only once the whole street can read them.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The extension does not change the underlying security issues of BGP except in two cases. First, inconsistency between AS_PATH and AS4_PATH can lose AS path information and cause routing loops in some cases, which an attacker could exploit. Second, using a non-mappable four-octet number as a Confederation member AS before all speakers have upgraded is a misconfiguration that weakens loop detection inside the Confederation.
sections.eli5: If the two copies of a path disagree, a router might get confused and send mail in circles, so everyone should keep their labels consistent.
